# Approve a remote work location change

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before a worker starts working from a different country or location with new legal, tax or security implications. A documented location decision and approved employment, payroll, immigration and security arrangements.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Gather the proposed location and working facts

agent-runnable


Record the employing entity, worker status, current and proposed locations, dates, duties and customer or data access. Distinguish temporary travel from a permanent relocation and keep identity records private.

- Sources: [GOV.UK structure your business overseas](https://www.business.gov.uk/export-from-uk/support-topics/routes-to-market-and-operating-overseas/structure-your-business-overseas/) · [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Assess local employment, tax and immigration implications

human · human approval required


Qualified advisers review the worker's authorization, payroll, employer obligations and entity exposure. Identify facts that could change the conclusion and keep the move unapproved while a required determination is unresolved.

- Sources: [GOV.UK structure your business overseas](https://www.business.gov.uk/export-from-uk/support-topics/routes-to-market-and-operating-overseas/structure-your-business-overseas/) · [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the operating and cost alternatives

agent-runnable


Compare the approved employment, EOR or entity routes, costs, supervision, time zones and data-access constraints. Link the chosen route to the existing cross-border hiring or entity process rather than assuming a laptop makes the move compliant.

- Sources: [GOV.UK structure your business overseas](https://www.business.gov.uk/export-from-uk/support-topics/routes-to-market-and-operating-overseas/structure-your-business-overseas/) · [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve the arrangement and required documents

human · human approval required


The authorized company and worker review the final location, duration, terms and conditions. Obtain required permissions and registrations through their own processes before the approved start date.

- Sources: [GOV.UK structure your business overseas](https://www.business.gov.uk/export-from-uk/support-topics/routes-to-market-and-operating-overseas/structure-your-business-overseas/) · [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Verify implementation and monitor changes

agent-runnable


Reconcile payroll, access, equipment and responsible contacts with the decision. Calendar the review or end date and reassess extensions or changes in duties, location or entity.

- Verify: A documented location decision and approved employment, payroll, immigration and security arrangements.
- Sources: [GOV.UK structure your business overseas](https://www.business.gov.uk/export-from-uk/support-topics/routes-to-market-and-operating-overseas/structure-your-business-overseas/) · [Acas inductions](https://www.acas.org.uk/inductions)
